prompt: Let's do a PR review. A teammate's stream job consumes ad clicks from Kafka, aggregates them into per-ad 1-minute tumbling windows, and on each window flush writes one row per (adId, windowStart) into a ClickHouse table that backs the analytics dashboard — the dashboard just sums click counts per ad. Kafka delivery here is at-least-once, so if the aggregator crashes right after a flush and restarts, it will replay and re-flush that same window. Walk me through this table DDL, the flush INSERT, and the read query out loud as if you're reviewing the PR — is this correct, and if not, what's the fix?
givenCode:
-- ============================================================
-- PR: ad_click_counts table + flush write path + dashboard read
-- ============================================================

-- 1) TABLE DDL
-- One row is written per (adId, windowStart) every time a 1-minute
-- tumbling window flushes.
CREATE TABLE ad_click_counts
(
    adId        String,
    windowStart DateTime,   -- start of the 1-minute tumbling window
    count       UInt64,     -- clicks aggregated for this ad in this window
    version     UInt64,     -- flush attempt counter, written but never read anywhere below
    flushedAt   DateTime DEFAULT now()  -- also written but never read anywhere below
)
ENGINE = MergeTree()
ORDER BY (adId, windowStart);

-- 2) FLUSH / WRITE PATH
-- Called once by the aggregator whenever a per-ad 1-minute window closes.
-- Kafka consumption is at-least-once: if the process crashes right after
-- this statement runs and restarts, the same window gets replayed and
-- this exact INSERT fires again for the same (adId, windowStart) — there
-- is no upsert, no existence check, no dedup before the write.
INSERT INTO ad_click_counts (adId, windowStart, count, version, flushedAt)
VALUES
    ('ad_123', '2026-07-19 10:05:00', 842, 1, now());

-- On crash + restart + Kafka replay of the SAME window, this runs again:
INSERT INTO ad_click_counts (adId, windowStart, count, version, flushedAt)
VALUES
    ('ad_123', '2026-07-19 10:05:00', 842, 2, now());
-- MergeTree has no replacement semantics on ORDER BY (adId, windowStart);
-- both rows now sit in the table side by side.

-- 3) READ / QUERY PATH — powers the analytics dashboard
-- Bare sum(count), no FINAL, no argMax(count, version): every row for
-- a given adId is added up, so the duplicate row from the re-flush above
-- is counted twice and the dashboard total for ad_123 comes out doubled.
SELECT
    adId,
    sum(count) AS totalClicks
FROM ad_click_counts
GROUP BY adId;
